new_statements.quote: O acento de altura é distintivo. Dentro das palavras, várias sílabas podem levar o tom alto. Fora isso, não sabemos muito sobre o sistema acentual do Kabiyari que pode ser parecido com o do Barasana (tukano). Exemplos de oposição: [...] núa vou / nuá meu dente; wápana nossa casa / wápaná plantamos [...] núuri socó-boi / nuúrí gripe / núri meu filho. [p.468:] - O Yukuna e o Kabiyari podem possuir vários acentos por morfema, mas a estrutura do sistema acentual ainda resta a fazer.
new_statements.translation: Pitch accent is distinctive. Within words, several syllables may carry high tone. Beyond that, we do not know much about the accentual system of Kabiyari, which may be similar to that of Barasana (Tukanoan). Examples of opposition: núa 'I go' / nuá 'my tooth'; wápana 'our house' / wápaná 'we plant'; núuri 'tiger heron' / nuúrí 'flu' / núri 'my son'. [p.468:] Yukuna and Kabiyari may have several accents per morpheme, but the structure of the accentual system still remains to be worked out.
new_statements.citation: Ramirez, Henri. 2001. Línguas Arawak da Amazônia Setentrional: Comparação e Descrição. Manaus: Editora da Universidade do Amazonas.

I re-extracted PDF pp. 396-397 (printed 386-387, sec. 4.4.1 'Fonologia' of 4.4 'Os Kabiyari') and p. 479 (printed 468, sec. 5.2) with extracted text and rendered p. 397 at 110 dpi to read the minimal-pair table. The quoted passage is present at the stated locators: p.386 l.42-43 'O acento de altura é distintivo. Dentro das palavras, várias sílabas podem levar o tom alto. Fora isso, não sabemos muito sobre o sistema acentual' / p.387 'do Kabiyari que pode ser parecido com o do Barasana (família tukano). Exemplos de oposição:' followed by…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Accent (realised as high pitch) is lexically contrastive in position and not predictable from word edges; a word may carry more than one high-toned syllable; the author explicitly says the system is otherwise undescribed and may be Barasana-like (tonal/pitch-accent). No fixed stress position is stated.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described; only the remark that several syllables per word (even per morpheme) may bear high tone/accent.
new_statements.exceptions: None; author flags the analysis as incomplete ('não sabemos muito', 'ainda resta a fazer').
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level citation forms from the author's own field notes (isolated words and short possessed/verb forms with person prefixes); acute marks high pitch on vowels, long vowels written double.
new_statements.identity_note: Ramirez 2001 describes 'Kabiyari' of the río Cananari (Apaporis tributary), c. 50 speakers, from his own field notes = Cabiyarí/Kawiyarí cabi1241 (ISO cbb); no dialect differentiation reported. SAPhon's divergent inventory (aspirates, retroflex, nasal vowels) comes from Reinoso Galindo 2009 on the same language.

sources.note: pp.386-387: pitch accent ('acento de altura') is distinctive; within a word several syllables may bear high tone; beyond that little is known of the Kabiyari accentual system, which may resemble Barasana (Tukanoan); minimal pairs núa 'vou' / nuá 'meu dente', wápana 'nossa casa' / wápaná 'plantamos', núuri / nuúrí / núri. p.468: Yukuna and Kabiyari may have several accents per morpheme, but the structure of the accentual system remains to be worked out (contrast: Achagua 2nd mora, Baniwa-Curripaco penultimate mora, Piapoco morphemic).
